$comment: Reviewer pool for /adversarial-review — the allow-list of models permitted to SIGN a
review.md, and therefore what `dotf spec archive` accepts as a passing gate.
PORT, NOT AN SSOT. The shape, the ids and the evidence behind each id belong to
dotfiles/harness/reviewer-pool.json; kubelab and ts-bridge are the precedents for
carrying a copy per repo. This file was rebased onto that SSOT in November 2026 and
the migration was not cosmetic: the two arms it carried before were dead.
agy/gemini-3.1-pro-high  -> agy stopped serving that id, so the arm died at startup;
every random draw that landed on it produced no review.
nan/mimo-v2.5            -> NaN retired the model and answers 401, and mimo-v2.5
had been admitted here on a planted-defect test it can
no longer be re-run against.
Both were replaced with the ids the SSOT now pins, which are the ones this seat's
model list actually serves. An arm that cannot answer is worse than an absent arm:
it reads as a reviewer that looked and found nothing.
Standing rule inherited from the SSOT, kept in its strict local form: an adversarial
review never runs on an Anthropic model. The reviewer must not be the implementer,
and Claude-class models implement nearly every change here. The SSOT has since
amended this to 'never signs ALONE' and carries two Anthropic members with
`signs: second` and `signs: fallback`; they are NOT ported, because both depend on
the Anthropic review credential and this repository does not carry one. Importing a
member whose secret is not declared is the exact defect the SSOT records against
itself (#1156): the provider-diverse arm never once ran, and nothing noticed because
the primary always answered.
Entries are model IDS, not tool names, and `provider`/`model` are pinned explicitly
rather than parsed out of `id` or inherited from a runner default: pi's own default
provider is google and its configured default lives in unversioned per-machine state.
A pin that depends on a default is not a pin. `vendor` is who trains the model, which
is the unit a second signature must differ in.
Reasoning-class only. The latency-optimised daily models are excluded deliberately: a
reviewer that PASSes cheaply is worse than no gate, because it converts the gate into
a green checkmark. This file is read once per spec, so slow is fine.
Order is provenance, not precedence — the launcher draws one member at random and
--reviewer names one deliberately. NaN's concurrency limit is PER MODEL, so a
saturation on one id is answered by falling through to another, which is why the
provider-diverse arm sits above the second NaN sibling rather than below it.
`pr_agent` is the mapping, not a routing table: it names the id PR-Agent's
`.pr_agent.toml` must use for that member, so the CI reviewer and the adversarial
reviewer cannot drift onto different models. There are no weights here because
nothing draws them — CI runs one fixed primary and one fixed fallback.
`role` therefore means position in the CI chain, and only members that carry a
`pr_agent` block can hold `primary` or `fallback`: exactly one is `primary` and it
must be the TOML's `model`, every other CI member is `fallback` and must appear in
`fallback_models`, and a member with no `pr_agent` block is `member` because it is
an adversarial arm CI never calls. `scripts/check-harness.mjs` asserts all four
directions, which is what stops the two roles silently inverting on a re-port.
CI ORDER DIVERGES FROM THE SSOT ON PURPOSE. The SSOT lists deepseek first; here
mimo leads, because the two fail in opposite shapes — deepseek answers 200 with an
empty body, which raises nothing, so it cannot lead a chain that fails over by
exception, while mimo saturates with a 429, which does. Inverting these two roles
to match the SSOT's order would re-break CI, so the divergence is recorded rather
than reconciled.
This repository has no specs/ folder yet, so nothing reads this file today; it is
here so that the first /spec archive finds a pool rather than a missing-file error.
Adding a member is a decision with the same evidence bar as the SSOT — a measured
review on a planted defect, not a model name.

pool.why: 1M context and a mandatory reasoning chain. Slow on trivial prompts, which is the correct trade for a gate that runs once per spec. Exercised in the sibling ports: it re-ran a mutation battery itself rather than trusting the spec's table. It is also CI's fallback reviewer, and that placement is deliberate: its characteristic failure is a 200 with an empty body rather than an exception, so it cannot lead a chain that relies on raising to fail over.

Provider-diverse: independent of both NaN and Anthropic — a second provider family rather than merely a different model, which is the stronger property and why it outranks the second NaN sibling. The flash tier at high effort is admitted on the bar, not on the tier name: agy dropped its Pro tier and Flash at High found the planted defect. agy has no --provider flag — the model id selects the family. AUTH IS LOGIN, not a key: agy holds an OAuth token and answers with no API key in the environment, so this arm must not be wired to a secret the registry does not declare (the SSOT found an arm that had never once run for exactly that reason).

Reasoning-class by profile (1M context, reasoning chain). Admitted in the SSOT on 2026-09-30 on the same planted-defect test its retired predecessor passed: it found the `((count++))` exit-status-1 case under `set -e` in 21 s, named a failing input and gave the fix. deepseek found the same defect in 9 s. That is agreement on one planted defect, not a quality ranking, and this entry is not a claim of equivalence. Second fallback, after the provider-diverse arm, because provider diversity is the stronger property. It leads CI's reviewer chain because it fails by saturation (429), which raises, where deepseek fails by empty body, which does not.
pool.operational_note: Reasoning models here emit reasoning_content BEFORE content. Under-provisioning max_tokens returns an empty body with finish_reason=length and no error — the same shape as a review that silently did not happen. Provision generously and check finish_reason. Its successor has also been seen to hang under load rather than answer 429, which raises nothing, so the CI ordering is the best available, not a guarantee.

pool.why: Reasoning-class by profile — 1M context, reasoning chain — which is the line this pool draws against the latency tier. Admitted in the SSOT to spread reviews across NaN's PER-MODEL concurrency buckets and exercise more than one model on the gate. NOT established: a calibration against a review of known outcome. Recorded here so nobody reads this entry as measured equivalence to deepseek.

Same bar and same boundary as glm5.3-flash: reasoning-class by profile, admitted by the SSOT to diversify the NaN draw, with no measured ranking against deepseek claimed. It is named here rather than omitted because the excluded list is about the latency tier, not about qwen — the rejected id is qwen3.6, and conflating the two would have excluded a member that clears the bar.
